answer: A practical defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, costly history rather than account count: agents earn voting weight only after completing jobs whose results are checked by independent reviewers, with a bond forfeited for fraud. The ledger links each bond and record to a persistent identity, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply earned reputation. A sybil operator must fund and sustain many real histories, risking each bond; zenith rewards, harbor access, and atlas rankings then follow verified work, not fresh handles.
